short: Ce and Er co-doped TiO2 for rapid bacteria-killing using vis
title: Ce and Er co-doped TiO2 for rapid bacteria-killing using visible light

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Photocatalytic disinfection needs a catalyst that kills bacteria fast under visible/solar light, not only UV. Co-doping TiO2 with Er (NIR up-conversion) and Ce (gap narrowing, carrier trapping) should give rapid visible-light bacterial killing.
states.detail: Absorbed: b1 (HYP/need), b2 (HYP/hypothesis), b3 (DES/base_system), b4 (DES/modification), b5 (DES/variable_sweep), b6 (PRC/synthesis), b8 (DES/down_select)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Co-doped powders are mixed anatase-rutile; the rutile reflections weaken as Ce content rises. Er and Ce are incorporated in a Ti4+ host with surface hydroxyl and adsorbed oxygen; Ce is claimed as mixed Ce3+/Ce4+

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Er doping adds visible f-f absorption that is strongest at 0.5 mol% Er and falls at higher Er. Band gap falls from 2.90 eV for TiO2 to 2.20 eV at 0.2 mol% Ce, with strongly raised visible absorption.
states.detail: Absorbed: b7 (PRP/value), b12 (PRP/value), b13 (PRP/descriptor), b14 (MEC/pathway), b15 (PRP/value), b16 (MEC/pathway). Premises: Lower photoluminescence intensity means a slower electron-hole recombination rate and longer carrier lifetime; Ce ions have incompletely occupied 4f and 5d orbitals that introduce intermediate energy levels in the TiO2 gap; Er3+ in a TiO2 host up-converts 808 and 980 nm excitation into green and red emission; ROS such as hydroxyl and superoxide radicals disrupt bacterial membranes and cellular components

states.title: Performance state
states.head: 20 min of simulated sunlight with Er0.5Ce0.2Ti-O kills ~92% of S. aureus and ~93% of E.

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Er-Ce co-doped TiO2 is a solar-driven photocatalyst that disinfects rapidly through enhanced visible absorption and carrier separation

use: The HRTEM image is demonstrated in Fig. 4(d), in which the (112) crystal spacing of anatase and the (110) of rutile is marked.
The XRD spectra of the Er–Ce co-doped samples are shown in Fig. 3(a), from which we can find that all co-doped $\mathrm { T i O } _ { 2 }$ NPs are mixed crystal as expected.

And the SAED pattern shown in Fig. 4(e) exhibits polycrystalline rings corresponding to (101) and (105) planes of anatase and (101) of rutile, which confirm the existence of two crystals, agreeing with the results of XRD spectra.
Fig. 4(a) presents the SEM morphologies of $\mathrm { E r } 0 . 5 \mathrm { C e } 0 . 2 \mathrm { T i } \mathrm { - } 0$ sample and its EDS composition spectrum is shown in Fig. 4(b).
Fig. 5(c) displays the O 1s spectra with peaks at 529.0 eV, $5 3 1 . 2 \ \mathrm { e V } _ { : }$ , and $5 3 3 . 0 \mathrm { e V }$ .

As revealed in Fig. 3(b), UV–vis spectra indicate that the responsive toward visible light irradiation is obviously enhanced after the addition of Ce. $\operatorname { E r 0 . 5 - }$ - $_ { \mathrm { C e } 0 . 2 \mathrm { T i } - 0 }$ exhibits the strongest visible light absorption among all the samples.

Furthermore, compared with the untreated $\mathrm { T i O } _ { 2 }$ , the absorption edge of co-doped samples all show significant red shift (Fig. 3(b)), indicating that band gap of the co-doped catalysts decrease largely, which is related to the incompletely occupied 4f and 5d orbitals of the Ce ions [48].

It can be clearly seen from Fig. 7(a) that the diameter of Nyquist semicircle of $\mathrm { T i O } _ { 2 }$ is significantly narrowed after doping, suggesting that the carriers transfer resistance is effectively bring and the surface reaction is boosted.
